## Context

Test isolation under ~90-worktree/xdist parallelism is 15.8% of the defect stream (R2S1). The harness root already exists and propagates: `tests/conftest.py:486-513` provides the session-scoped `_rebar_root_sandbox_repo` and an autouse fixture that `monkeypatch.setenv("REBAR_ROOT", ...)`, per-worker under xdist via `tmp_path_factory`. Propagation to children is by **environment inheritance**, so a test that builds its own `env=` dict from scratch silently drops `REBAR_ROOT` and the child falls back to the git toplevel of cwd — the real checkout.

What is missing is ENFORCEMENT: nothing stops a new unit-tier test from spawning a subprocess with its own ad-hoc temp/HOME/root, which is how the recent class instances arose (`82a0d5cd`: a `home=Path.home()` default reached transitively, resolving the operator's real home; `ef9e1d74`: a single subprocess wall-clock bound conflating a product deadline with machine slack). Precedent: pip's `pytest_collection_modifyitems` raising on forbidden patterns; Bazel's hermetic `TEST_TMPDIR` contract (12c) recorded as the escalation path.

## Approach

A fourth arm in the existing `pytest_collection_modifyitems` (`tests/conftest.py:220`), delegating to a **pure predicate** in a new `tests/_subprocess_isolation.py` — mirroring the `_live_jira_confinement` split, so the predicate is unit-testable without spawning pytest.

Detection is **AST, not regex**: resolve `ast.Call` sites whose callee binds to `subprocess.{run,Popen,check_output,check_call,call}`, `os.system`, `os.popen`, or `pytest.main`, resolving module aliases from the file's own imports. Regex is disqualified — a naive `run(` pattern matches 126 `asyncio.run` sites.

The census on the current tier is 866 spawn sites across 334 files, of which ~841 already take their root from the harness (`cwd=<fixture path>`, `git -C <fixture path>`, a positional `git init <tmp_path>`, `env=subprocess_env(...)`, or plain env inheritance). Only ~26 are hazards, in three shapes: an `env=` dict literal carrying neither `os.environ` nor `REBAR_ROOT` (3), `cwd=REPO_ROOT`/`git -C REPO_ROOT` (23), and one site reading the operator's `$HOME`.

**Bounding the check conservatively is a requirement, not a nicety.** Roughly 58 sites pass `env=<bare variable>` and are undecidable without a def-site trace; these are REPORTED, never failed — failing them would redden 42 files on day one. The sanctioned nested-pytest funnel `tests/_nested_pytest.py` and its four documented exceptions are exempt by name.

Failures raise `pytest.UsageError`, not `pytest.fail`: this arm can fire from the xdist controller, where a `pytest.fail` escapes as a 20-line `INTERNALERROR>` traceback — the precedent and its rationale are already recorded at `tests/conftest.py:264-274` ("a guard whose whole value is a clear message must not look like a crash").

The opt-out is `@pytest.mark.allow_unharnessed_subprocess("<reason>")`. `--strict-markers` validates only the marker NAME, so the mandatory-reason rule is enforced by the guard itself (empty/blank args fail collection) — the same "reason is mandatory" convention as `# read-via:` in `check_config_reads.py`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: collection fails with an instructive error naming the fixture to use, when a unit-tier test spawns a subprocess without taking its root from the harness. Verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_collection_isolation_guard.py`, which drives the predicate over a seeded violation fixture.
- [ ] AC2: the full unit tier collects clean at introduction, with the ~26 hazard sites fixed or explicitly marked and no blanket opt-out. Verified by `pytest --collect-only -q tests/unit` exiting 0.
- [ ] AC3: the guard raises `pytest.UsageError` (not `pytest.fail`) so an xdist-controller failure reads as a clean `ERROR:` banner. Verified by a test asserting the raised type.
- [ ] AC4: the opt-out marker requires a non-blank reason string, and a bare or empty-reason marker fails collection. Verified by a test over both forms.
- [ ] AC5: opt-out growth is greppable and countable, so the mechanism ratchet can see it. Verified by `grep -rn "allow_unharnessed_subprocess" tests/ | wc -l` returning the marked-site count.
- [ ] AC6: statically undecidable `env=<bare variable>` sites are reported, not failed. Verified by a test asserting such a site yields a report entry and no collection failure.
- [ ] AC7: the check and the marker are documented alongside the existing isolation helpers.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/unit/test_collection_isolation_guard.py -v` — the guard's own suite: seeded violation fires (AC1), `UsageError` type (AC3), marker reason required (AC4), undecidable site reported not failed (AC6). The predicate is exercised directly, so no nested pytest spawn is needed.
- `pytest --collect-only -q tests/unit` — proves the tier collects clean at introduction (AC2).
- `pytest -n 4 --collect-only -q tests/unit` — proves the controller path renders the message cleanly rather than as an INTERNALERROR (AC3).
- `grep -rn "allow_unharnessed_subprocess" tests/ | wc -l` — the countable opt-out census (AC5).
- `make lint && make typecheck` — house gates stay green.

## File impact

- `tests/_subprocess_isolation.py` (new; the pure AST predicate, unit-testable in isolation)
- `tests/conftest.py` (fourth arm in `pytest_collection_modifyitems`; register the marker in `pytest_configure`)
- `tests/unit/test_collection_isolation_guard.py` (new; seeded-violation RED proof and the marker/undecidable cases)
- the ~26 hazard sites fixed or marked (final set from the AST census)
- `docs/` (the testing/isolation section documenting the existing guards)
